question.problem: The function $f(x)=\frac{1}{7x+k}$ has an inverse function given by ${f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1+3x}{7x}.$ What is the value of $k?$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{1}{7x+k}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{1}{7y+k}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{1}{7y+k} \\ x(7y+k) & =1 \\ 7xy+kx & =1 \\ 7xy & =1-kx \\ y & =\frac{1-kx}{7x}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{1-kx}{7x}.
$$

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=-3.$
